stemMd: How much heat raises 0.5 kg of water by 4 degrees Celsius? Use specific heat 4200 J/(kg degree Celsius) and neglect losses.
explanationMd: Heat is mcΔT=0.5 times 4200 times 4=8400 J. Specific heat is energy per mass per degree, so both the mass and temperature change must be included.

distractorRationale.d: This uses 1 kg instead of 0.5 kg.
distractorRationale.e: This divides by temperature rise instead of multiplying.
distractorRationale.a: This uses the specific heat as the total energy.
